changelog: C4 changed to add a concise operational rule addressing the finding that short adjuncts/parentheticals and leading function-word fragments should not automatically raise contra when the prefix already conveys a self-contained assertion; this makes the contra check explicit and actionable.
Replaced example E1 with the measured labeled example en_us_733 (Whistler sentence) so scorers see a real short-adjunct case and learn to prefer isolating self-contained prefixes.
Paraphrased C4 to be much shorter while keeping the new low-contra guidance for short adjuncts/parentheticals; addresses finding that scorers overestimate contradiction risk for short continuations.
Paraphrased C6 to a more concise cohesion checklist to save space while preserving guidance about dependencies crossing cuts; supports finding about attachment and orphaning.
Paraphrased C8 to shorten wording about applying both judgements and using English tendencies only as soft guidance; reduces overall prompt length.
Replaced E1 with the Whistler example from the critique to correct example-driven bias toward unsafe singleton fragments and illustrate low-contra for parentheticals.
Replaced E2 with the Pacific Tsunami example from the critique to further correct example-driven biases about single-token continuations and scope.
Deleted E3 (the previous 'Humans can be affected...' example) to reduce prompt size and remove an example that contributed to miscalibration.

Replace hand-written pyramid example (E1) with a measured short-adjunct case (en_us_1294) so scorers see a real example where an early self-contained prefix has low contra; this targets the finding that short continuations/leading function words were being over-weighted.
Delete example E2 (Costello/Whistler-style placeholder) because it contributed to example-driven bias toward singleton function-word cuts and to prompt over-length.
Delete example E3 (Humans affected... example) to further remove misleading guidance and bring the prompt back under the size budget.
